security: Mandatory AUTHORITY-CHECK before any data modification (INSERT, UPDATE, MODIFY, DELETE) or sensitive data display.
Always check sy-subrc = 0 immediately after AUTHORITY-CHECK statement.
Never use dynamic SQL concatenation that accepts unsanitized user inputs to prevent SQL Injection.
Avoid hardcoding passwords, API tokens, client secrets, or user credentials in source code.

This enters the picture, for example, in the context of ABAP SQL. Since ABAP SQL statements do not trigger any authorization checks in the database system, this is even more important. Database tables may be accessed without restriction using these statements. Conversely, not all users in a system are authorized to access all data available to ABAP SQL statements.
Thus, it is up to the programmer to ensure that each user who can call the program is authorized to access the data it handles.
performance: Never execute SELECT, SELECT SINGLE, or database queries inside LOOP ... ENDLOOP (N+1 query problem). Use FOR ALL ENTRIES IN or set-based SELECTs.
Never execute UPDATE, MODIFY, DELETE on database tables inside LOOPs without batching.
Always specify primary key or secondary index fields in WHERE clauses to prevent full table scans.
Avoid SELECT *; specify only the required columns to minimize network bandwidth and database memory usage.
Acquire exclusive lock via ENQUEUE_<lock_object> before database mutations and release via DEQUEUE_<lock_object> / COMMIT WORK.

Ensure that statements are placed in the appropriate position (e.g. within loops, conditions). Avoid unnecessary executions of statements (e.g. redundant processing, redundant select single statements in loops).
Avoid unnecessary or repeated method calls if the return value does not change (e.g. getting the date, time, UUID, etc.).
Internal tables and deep structures with large amounts of data should not be passed by value.
Use primary and secondary table keys wisely. Avoid linear searches on large tables.
Use CDS views instead of joining multiple large tables via Open SQL when possible.
clean_abap_and_modern_syntax: In ABAP RAP (RESTful Application Programming), never use direct SQL DML (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) on managed tables; use EML (Entity Manipulation Language: MODIFY ENTITIES / READ ENTITIES).
Use modern inline declarations DATA(var) and FINAL(var) instead of obsolete top-of-routine DATA statements.
Use constructor expressions (VALUE, CORRESPONDING, COND, SWITCH, REDUCE, FILTER) instead of manual loops and work areas.
Replace obsolete statements: TABLES, MOVE ... TO, COMPUTE, FORM / PERFORM (use Methods), RANGES (use types).
Prefer CDS View Entities (DEFINE VIEW ENTITY) over obsolete CDS DDIC-based views (DEFINE VIEW with @AbapCatalog.sqlViewName).
transport_and_activation: Detect breaking changes in interface definitions, method signatures (added mandatory parameters, changed types), or removed public methods.
Ensure dependent CDS View Entities, Data Elements, Domains, and Table definitions are activated and included in the same Transport Request.
Verify syntax compatibility with target SAP Release level (ABAP Cloud Language Version vs Standard ABAP).
